LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 INTERROGATIVES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: when clauses with present tense to show the future, for example, ‘When are you going to school?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify interrogatives in print or digital texts
2. use interrogatives correctly to express different meanings

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives

Teach
• Focus skill: identify interrogatives in print or digital texts.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when clauses with present tense to show the future, for example, ‘When are you going to school?
2. How do you form questions?
3. Why do we ask questions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
